messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty — AUTH_PROXY anomaly detected (alert_id=A-90321). 3.8k requests in 2m to /v1/auth, source IP cluster 203.0.113.0/24, error spike 401->500. Escalation level: P1.
priya-sre: acked. oncall? I see repeated svc-token echoes in debug logs. possible leaked debug header.
maria-oncall: taking this. paging incident channel. pulling runbook (auth-leak-runbook). @sam-eng can you confirm whether this is traffic from external client or internal telemetry?
sam-eng: quick check — logs show repeated requests with header `X-Debug-Id: svc-` and bodies containing `svcacct_id` fields. IPs are from a set of cloud scanners (203.0.113.45, 203.0.113.67). Not matching known customers. Likely external probing + some downstream service accidentally logging tokens. snippet from log:```
2025-06-14T15:23:02Z auth-proxy INFO request_id=abc123 src=203.0.113.45 path=/v1/auth status=200 latency_ms=12 headers={Authorization: REDACTED, X-Debug-Id: svc-temp-9, User-Agent: curl/7.86}
2025-06-14T15:23:02Z auth-proxy DEBUG payload={"svcacct_id":"svc-34a2","token_fragment":"eyJhbGci..."}
```
sam-eng: also seeing an S3 backup job that captured debug logs around 15:20 in staging-bak-logs. investigating bucket ACLs now.
alex-sec: cc @maria-oncall. immediate actions: 1) WAF block IP range 203.0.113.0/24; 2) short-term rate-limit auth-proxy to mitigate exfil; 3) rotate any svcacct keys that appear in logs; 4) preserve evidence (don't rotate until we snapshot and hand to IR if needed).
jessica-support: flagging support — do we have any customers impacted or exposed keys for customer-managed resources?
tyler-legal: holding — if there is potential PII or customer credential exposure, please pause any auto-deletion and preserve audit logs. Legal on standby.
maria-oncall: executing WAF rule now and enabling stricter rate-limit on auth-proxy routes. @sam-eng can you snapshot the staging-bak-logs bucket and set object lock for 24h? we need preserve.
sam-eng: snapshot started: `aws s3 cp s3://staging-bak-logs s3://forensics-snapshots/1747123456 --recursive --metadata x-preserve=true`
sam-eng: Found ~120 lines with token_fragment in staging backup. I will redact before wider distribution. For immediate containment, recommend revoking tokens for svcacct ids seen: svc-34a2, svc-7b9c, svc-001f.
priya-sre: runbook note — rotate service account keys (playbook id: rotate-svcacct-v2). Will follow controlled rotation: snapshot -> rotate -> verify -> publish new creds to consumers.
alex-sec: Also create temporary allowlist for internal telemetry IPs to avoid breaking ingestion. We'll need to coordinate with infra to update flows.
maria-oncall: Maria -> initiating key rotation plan in staging to validate: run `./ops/rotate_keys.sh --svc svc-34a2 --env staging` then escalate to prod if checks pass. tagging incident with #forensics.
sam-eng: ran rotation in staging (invoked script). logs: `rotate_keys.sh: rotated svc-34a2 -> new_key_id=k-8f7a; updated KMS alias; published to secrets-manager-staging`. No downstream errors observed in 2m.
jessica-support: notified account managers to monitor customer buckets. No tickets yet.
alex-sec: hold on full prod rotation until forensics snapshot completed (we have it) and IR says OK to rotate. But we should pre-stage rotation for prod during low traffic window.
tyler-legal: thanks. please add any affected customer IDs to this thread if found.
priya-sre: For immediate risk — we believe this was a probing scanner that caused accidental debug logging. No confirmed customer token misuse. We will proceed with controlled rotation for the three svcaccnts and revoke active sessions.
maria-oncall: revoking sessions now via admin API: `curl -X POST https://admin.internal/api/v1/sessions/revoke -d '{"svc_ids":["svc-34a2","svc-7b9c","svc-001f"]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>'`
maria-oncall: sessions revoked. WAF blocks active. Rate-limits applied. Staging bucket snapshot preserved.
sam-eng: created issue infra#8942 to remediate logging level bug where debug logs include token fragments. Patch inbound: PR #1028 updates logger to redact token_fragment fields at parse time.
alex-sec: Open action items: (A) rotate prod keys (prestage); (B) patch logger and deploy to staging then prod; (C) run audit of all buckets with debug logs in last 30d; (D) notify affected customers if any confirmed.
priya-sre: timeline so far: 15:20 alert -> 15:23 WAF/rate-limit -> 15:25 snapshot started -> 15:29 staging rotation validated -> 15:30 sessions revoked.
jessica-support: creating a CS internal note template in case customers ask. tagging support-runbook.
maria-oncall: handing over to daytime oncall @priya-sre for follow-up and postmortem. I’ll update the incident tracker with timeline + actions. :white_check_mark:
priya-sre: taking post-incident follow-up. will schedule a 30m incident review with eng, sec, legal, support. assigning owners for audit and full prod rotation.
tyler-legal: available for the review.
alex-sec: adding severity and classification to incident tracker: potential sensitive-data-exposure (SDE) — but no confirmed external compromise.
priya-sre: closing live mitigation channel for now. If new evidence appears, reopen paging. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
